text:
The reported 2021 loss was 81.3 hectares. Two independent forest maps support the pre-loss forest classification:

- The European Commission’s JRC map classified **98% of the loss area as forest in 2020**.
- Uruguay’s 2021 national forest map classified **68.1 hectares as planted pine forest**, none as native forest, and 13.2 hectares as outside mapped forest.

A later year was also observed in the annual series, which extends through 2025. Together with the JRC agreement, this meets the tool’s corroboration rule. The independent maps support the area’s forest status, though they do not by themselves establish the cause of the loss.
